title: Natural Language Autoencoders Identify Without Explaining
abstract: arXiv:2610.32691v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) express a model's internal activations in the form of readable text. The verbalizer turns an activation into an English explanation; the reconstructor then converts that explanation back into an activation, and the explanation is considered successful if the round trip brings back the original activation. We claim that this criterion evaluates whether the information is sufficient and does not address descriptive faithfulness. A sentence can contain sufficient information to make it possible to identify an activation even if it wrongly explains what the activation does: in the case of reconstruction, the primary aim is to accurately identify the activations and not to describe them. translated_title: 自然语言自编码器：识别而非解释
translated_abstract: 自然语言自编码器（NLA）以可读文本的形式表达模型的内部激活。言语化器将激活转换为英文解释；重建器随后将该解释转换回激活，如果这一往返过程能够恢复原始激活，则该解释被认为是成功的。我们主张这一标准仅评估了信息是否充分，而未涉及描述的忠实性。一句话可以包含足以识别某个激活的充分信息，即使它错误地解释了该激活的功能：在重建的场景中，首要目标是准确识别激活，而非描述它们。这一问题与思维链忠实性问题具有相同的结构——在该问题中，经过训练以伴随某一过程的言语输出被当作对该过程的报告，并且它类似于……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文指出自然语言自编码器（NLA）的往返重建成功标准只能证明解释性文本包含足以识别激活的信息，并不能保证该解释对激活实际功能的描述是忠实的，这一问题与思维链忠实性问题结构相同。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that the round-trip reconstruction criterion of Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) only shows that the verbal explanation contains sufficient information to identify an activation, but does not guarantee its descriptive faithfulness—an issue structurally parallel to the chain-of-thought faithfulness problem.
